claim: The trap is the name: Austria's 'Veltliner' grapes (Roter, Frühroter, Brauner, Grüner) are a family only on the label, and Grüner is not a Silvaner relative despite a century of textbooks saying so.
because: The key (Traminer × St. Georgener-Rebe) is right, but two statements in the explanation are false. Silvaner is Traminer × Österreichisch Weiss (per DNA fingerprinting), so Silvaner and Grüner Veltliner share Traminer as a parent and are half-siblings. Some of the Veltliners are also related to each other: Frühroter Veltliner is Roter Veltliner × Silvaner, a parent and child. What is true is that Grüner has no known link to Roter or Frühroter Veltliner. A smaller point: the St. Georgen vine was found in 2000 and the parentage was confirmed by DNA only in 2007, not 'shortly after'.
fix: The trap is the name: Grüner has no known genetic link to Roter, Frühroter or Brauner Veltliner, despite the shared label. Silvaner is not a parent either, though it is a half-sibling, since Silvaner is Traminer × Österreichisch Weiss. (Parent vine found in 2000; parentage confirmed by DNA in 2007.)
